markets.rules_primary: If the Bitcoin spot price according to the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index is above $100000.00 starting Jul 21, 2026 and before Nov 1, 2026 at 12:00 AM ET, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: The market resolves based on the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index (BRTI) using a trimmed mean calculation. The resolution value is calculated by taking all BRTI values for each minute from market issuance until the specified time on the target date, removing the top 20% and bottom 20% of values, then averaging the remaining 60% of values. If the BRTI crosses the threshold at any point during the measurement period (triggering early expiration), the market immediately resolves. If no data is available at the expiration time, the market resolves to No. The market can resolve early if Bitcoin definitively crosses the threshold before the target date and time.

markets.rules_primary: If the White House officially announces that it will end its access bans on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico after Issuance and before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only reporting from the White House qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

The qualifying publication must announce a definite White House decision that the access bans on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico will end, be lifted, terminated, or rescinded, including a definite future restoration. A statement covering only one or two outlets, merely acknowledging a court order, or saying the White House will comply temporarily while continuing to challenge the order does not qualify. Decisions about the Associated Press's access do NOT count.
markets.title: Will the White House announce an end to its press ban before Nov 1, 2026?

markets.rules_primary: If the United States and Iran hold a senior-level diplomatic meeting after Issuance and before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify, unless the new article itself explicitly reaffirms the truth of the topic as of the publication date. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

The meeting must be deliberately convened for diplomacy or negotiation, and each country must be represented by at least one senior official who actively participates in an official capacity. It need not produce an agreement, joint statement, or commitment to further talks. Only the part of a meeting held after Issuance counts; a meeting held entirely before Issuance does not qualify, even if reported afterward.

A senior official is a head of state or government, vice president, foreign minister or other cabinet-rank minister, head of a national security council, presiding officer of a national legislature, special envoy, or anyone the head of state or government designates to conduct diplomatic negotiations on their behalf. Officials whose mandate is limited to technical, implementation, monitoring, staff-level, or preparatory discussions do not qualify. Qualifying officials include, without limitation, Donald Trump, JD Vance, Marco Rubio, Scott Bessent, Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner for the United States, and Mojtaba Khamenei, Masoud Pezeshkian, Abbas Araghchi, and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf for Iran.

The meeting may be direct, with the officials meeting face to face in person (interpreters permitted), or indirect, with both delegations physically present in the same facility, venue, or city for a single organized round of talks and an intermediary authorized by both governments relaying communications between them on the same calendar day in the meeting location's local time.

Phone or video contact, chance encounters, and exchanges limited to greetings, courtesies, or photo opportunities do not qualify, nor do the proceedings of standing international organizations or recurring multilateral summits such as the UN General Assembly. A separately arranged bilateral meeting held alongside such an event may qualify. A meeting does not qualify if either country is represented only by persons lacking authority to conduct diplomacy or negotiation on its behalf. The incidental presence of supporting staff does not by itself disqualify a meeting.
markets.title: Will the U.S. and Iran hold a senior-level meeting before Nov 1, 2026?

markets.rules_primary: If Donald Trump has taken action by personally signing an executive order, presidential memorandum, proclamation, directive, determination, or finding adopting or directing adoption of a replacement for a preexisting official name, or restoring or directing restoration of a prior official name, for United States use after Issuance and before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The qualifying action must be of the specific type designated (executive order, presidential memorandum, proclamation, directive, determination, or finding), be signed by the President personally during the specified time period, and explicitly address the topic in the document's operative provisions, title, or official White House summary. Actions must have legal or policy effect - ceremonial proclamations without policy impact do not qualify unless specifically included. Actions that only incidentally mention the topic, statements without formal action, actions by cabinet members, legislative proposals without executive action, and signing statements do not qualify. The action must be publicly announced or documented by a Source Agency before expiration.

A qualifying presidential action must adopt or direct adoption of a replacement for a preexisting official name, or restore or direct restoration of a prior official name, for United States use. Initially naming a previously unnamed subject does not qualify. A reversion or reinstatement of a prior name qualifies. Merely authorizing a secondary, alternate, honorary, or informal title does not qualify unless the action directs replacement of the preexisting official name. A map, database, registry, contract, or other record change by USGS, the U.S. Board on Geographic Names, the Department of the Interior, or another agency does not qualify without the President's qualifying action.
markets.title: Will Trump take another official renaming action?

markets.rules_primary: If President Donald Trump gives his next qualifying address to the nation, as defined in Additional Details after Issuance and before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only reporting from at least four of the seven Source Agencies named in Additional Details qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify, unless the new article itself explicitly reaffirms the truth of the topic as of the publication date. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

An “address to the nation” means a prepared presidential speech that at least four of the Associated Press, Reuters, Bloomberg News, ABC, CBS, NBC, and The New York Times contemporaneously describe as an “address to the nation,” “national address,” “address to the American people,” or explicitly equivalent. At least two of ABC, CBS, and NBC must televise the speech nationwide, beginning within 60 seconds of its initial public transmission and continuing through the final prepared words. The speech may be delivered live or prerecorded. Examples include an update on Operation Epic Fury (4/1/26) and a year-end address on the economy and administration’s record (12/17/25).

The examples are illustrative only; qualification is determined solely by the definition above. A qualifying description must be published after the initial public transmission begins and must affirm that the address is underway or occurred. Advance descriptions of a planned speech do NOT qualify.

For deadline purposes, an address occurs when its initial public transmission begins. A strike can resolve Yes only if the transmission begins and all four qualifying descriptions are published before that strike date. Required network carriage may continue through the final prepared words after the strike date, but must be verified before determination.
markets.title: Will it be reported by at least four of the seven Source Agencies named in Additional Details that President Donald Trump gives his next qualifying address to the nation, as defined in Additional Details before Nov 1, 2026?

A meeting is defined as any of the following:

An in-person encounter where both parties are physically present in the same location
A virtual meeting via video conference where both parties can see and hear each other in real-time
A phone call where both parties speak directly to each other
Any combination of the above where the parties interact directly in real-time

The following qualify as meetings (though this list is not exhaustive):

Formal bilateral meetings, summits, or conferences
Informal encounters at multilateral events if documented by Source Agencies
Working dinners, lunches, or other meal meetings
Pull-aside meetings or corridor conversations if documented
Home visits or meetings at non-official locations

The following do NOT qualify as meetings:

Being present at the same event without direct interaction
Exchanging written correspondence
Communication through intermediaries without direct contact
Pre-recorded messages or asynchronous communication
Meetings cancelled after being scheduled
Near-misses where parties were scheduled to meet but did not

markets.rules_primary: If Serbia agrees to or announces a formal decision by the Speaker of the National Assembly calling the election for President of Serbia before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
An agreement or announcement qualifies if it involves any of the following:

Formal signing of treaties
Parliamentary approval with binding effect
Official ratification
Formal commitment by the head of state/government with constitutional authority
Official statements by authorized ministers
Official press releases
Formal declarations during government proceedings
Official statements to international bodies

Phased implementation announcements and multi-party agreements where the country is a signatory also qualify.

The following do NOT qualify:

Preliminary discussions
Conditional agreements contingent on circumstances
Opposition party statements
Leaked documents
Think-tank recommendations
General aspirations without specific commitment
Draft legislation without approval
Regional actions (unless specified)
Retraction of previously announced commitments

The decision calling the election for President of Serbia must be issued by the Speaker of the National Assembly, including a Speaker serving as acting President, and must set the voting date. Statements of intent, planned or expected dates, and statements by parties, the Government or other officials do not qualify unless they officially record that the decision has been issued. The decision counts if it is signed or officially announced after Issuance and before the market's date.
markets.title: Will Serbia call its presidential election before Nov 1, 2026?

Russian-origin diesel fuel is diesel fuel produced in Russia. Diesel fuel refined in another country from Russian crude oil is not Russian-origin diesel fuel.

Diesel fuel is imported into the United States when it is physically delivered to a U.S. port, or otherwise into U.S. territory, for commercial or government use within the United States. An import counts regardless of whether it is made under the Oct 9, 2026 agreement between the United States and Russia, General License 135 or any other authorization.

A purchase, contract, loading or voyage of Russian-origin diesel fuel to the United States, before it is actually delivered

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the function is implemented.
markets.rules_primary: If an OpenAI product has implemented a general-purpose personal AI agent that remembers the user and starts multi-step tasks across third-party apps on its own before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release.

A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (1) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (2) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user.

The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (1) and (2) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.
markets.title: Will OpenAI release a personal AI agent before Nov 1, 2026?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If the Prime Minister of Canada has personally and officially announced a new decision made after Issuance committing Canada to impose a new Canadian tariff or increase an existing Canadian tariff on U.S. goods after Issuance and before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only reporting from the Prime Minister of Canada qualifies for the purposes of this market. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

The publication must expressly commit Canada to impose a new Canadian tariff or increase an existing Canadian tariff on U.S. goods. It must be an official speech, statement, or press release issued personally or in the prime minister's name. A specified future effective date qualifies.

Minister- or agency-only announcements, negotiating objectives, noncommittal statements of intent that do not expressly commit Canada, general aspirations, preliminary discussions, threats, conditional proposals, and the automatic activation or expiry of a previously announced measure do NOT qualify. A new decision to reimpose a previously removed tariff or increase an existing tariff qualifies. Reports merely referencing publications before Issuance do NOT qualify unless they explicitly reaffirm a qualifying new decision made after Issuance.
markets.title: Will the Prime Minister of Canada announce new or increased tariffs on U.S. goods before Nov 1, 2026?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If the Prime Minister of Canada has personally and officially announced a new decision made after Issuance committing Canada to reduce, remove, or suspend an existing Canadian tariff on U.S. goods after Issuance and before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only reporting from the Prime Minister of Canada qualifies for the purposes of this market. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

The publication must expressly commit Canada to reduce, remove, or suspend an existing Canadian tariff on U.S. goods. It must be an official speech, statement, or press release issued personally or in the prime minister's name. A specified future effective date qualifies.

Minister- or agency-only announcements, negotiating objectives, noncommittal statements of intent that do not expressly commit Canada, general aspirations, preliminary discussions, threats, conditional proposals, and the automatic activation or expiry of a previously announced measure do NOT qualify. A new decision reversing an earlier tariff policy qualifies only if it reduces, removes, or suspends an existing tariff. Reports merely referencing publications before Issuance do NOT qualify unless they explicitly reaffirm a qualifying new decision made after Issuance.
markets.title: Will the Prime Minister of Canada announce lower tariffs on U.S. goods before Nov 1, 2026?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If any New York State court invalidates, annuls, or enjoins Nikki Lucas's election as chair of the Brooklyn Democratic Party, including by ordering a new election for that office or barring her from serving or acting as chair, in the Kings County Supreme Court litigation over the Brooklyn Democratic Party's leadership, any appeal of that litigation, or any other action challenging Lucas's election as chair before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The ruling must:
Be issued by any New York State court in the Kings County Supreme Court litigation over the Brooklyn Democratic Party's leadership, any appeal of that litigation, or any other action challenging Lucas's election as chair
Address the matter described by the specified judgment
Be issued through a written order, opinion, judgment, or decision

Partial relief counts. A written temporary restraining order, preliminary or permanent injunction, or stay whose operative terms bar Nikki Lucas from serving or acting as chair, or bar the Brooklyn Democratic Party from recognizing her as chair, qualifies even if it is interim or limited in scope.

A ruling that only voids the party's rule amendments or only decides who holds interim authority does not qualify unless it also invalidates or enjoins Lucas's election or service as chair. A written ruling that declares the Oct. 4, 2026 executive committee vote void or without effect, or that recognizes another person as the lawful chair for the same term, counts as invalidating Lucas's election. A qualifying ruling counts when issued, even if it is later stayed, vacated, or reversed.

The following do NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion:
Oral rulings from the bench unless reduced to a written order
Tentative rulings that are not made final
Draft opinions that leak but are not officially issued
Settlements or voluntary dismissals
Administrative or scheduling orders
Orders to show cause
Minute orders that do not address the substantive issue in the specified judgment

For clarity:
If the case is dismissed for lack of jurisdiction, that counts as a ruling only if the judgment refers to jurisdiction
Sua sponte rulings count if they match the specified judgment
Per curiam opinions and summary orders count as rulings
If multiple judges issue separate opinions, the majority/plurality opinion controls
markets.title: Will a court invalidate or enjoin Nikki Lucas's election as Brooklyn Dem chair?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the function is implemented.
markets.rules_primary: If an Anthropic product has implemented a general-purpose personal AI agent that remembers the user and starts multi-step tasks across third-party apps on its own before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release.

A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (1) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (2) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user.

The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (1) and (2) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.
markets.title: Will Anthropic release a personal AI agent before Nov 1, 2026?

markets.early_close_condition: If an event described in the Payout Criterion occurs, expiration will be moved to an earlier date and time in accordance with Rule 7.2.
markets.rules_primary: If any AI lab solves another Millennium Prize Problem after Issuance and before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A Millennium Prize Problem counts as solved on the first date that, by Expiration, remains unretracted and either:

A complete proof, disproof, or counterexample addressing the problem as originally formulated by the Clay Mathematics Institute is published in a reputable peer-reviewed mathematics or scientific journal.
CMI or another recognized academic governing or recognition body officially states that the problem has been resolved by reference to a specific written work.
At least two Source Agencies themselves report that the problem has been proven, disproven, or otherwise resolved by reference to a specific publicly available written work.

A preprint, announcement, blog post, conference presentation, technical report, or machine-checked formalization does NOT by itself constitute a solution, but may be the written work relied upon for official recognition or qualifying Source Agency reporting. Award of a Millennium Prize by CMI is NOT required.

Partial results, special cases, unrelated reformulations, results conditional on unproven assumptions, and findings that the problem is independent of or undecidable within its framework do NOT count. The result must establish the truth or falsity of the problem as originally formulated.

A solution is attributed to AI lab when Source Agencies report that AI lab, its personnel, or an AI system developed and operated by it produced the solution in whole or substantial part, and the lab or system is credited as an author, contributor, or producer. Collaborative work qualifies; independent third-party use of the lab's publicly available model or product without such participation or credit does NOT.

Each Millennium Prize Problem counts at most once. Problems solved before time period do NOT count. A purported solution that is retracted, withdrawn, repudiated, rescinded, disavowed, or reported to contain an unresolved identified error before Expiration does NOT count.
markets.title: Will any AI lab solve a Millennium Prize Problem before Nov 1, 2026?
